title: Rukmini Devi Temple - The Sacred Shrine of Krishna’s Queen in Dwarka
content:
Rukmini Devi Temple

The Rukmini Devi Temple, located just a few kilometers from Dwarka, Gujarat, is a sacred temple dedicated to Rukmini Devi, the consort of Lord Krishna. Though lesser-known compared to the grand Dwarkadhish Temple, this shrine holds deep mythological significance and is a must-visit for those on a spiritual journey through Dwarka.

It’s a place that not only offers peace and devotion but also a glimpse into ancient Indian mythology and temple architecture.

 Click here for packages

Location

Where: 2 km northeast of Dwarka city, Gujarat

Nearest Landmark: On the way to Bet Dwarka and Nageshwar Jyotirlinga

Distance from Dwarkadhish Temple: Approx. 2-3 km

Who is Rukmini Devi?

Rukmini Devi is considered the principal queen (Patrani) of Lord Krishna. She was the princess of Vidarbha and a form of Goddess Lakshmi, the goddess of wealth and prosperity.

Her devotion and love for Krishna are legendary, and her story symbolizes eternal love, humility, and sacrifice.

Temple History & Mythology

This temple is believed to be over 2,000 years old, with the current structure built around the 12th century in a classic Nagara architectural style.

Myth Behind the Temple

According to legend:

After their marriage, Krishna and Rukmini visited the sage Durvasa. On the way, Rukmini felt thirsty and asked Krishna for water. Krishna struck the ground with his toe, and the Ganga river appeared. Rukmini drank without offering water to Durvasa, which angered the sage. He cursed her to live separately from Krishna - this is why Rukmini Temple is located far from Dwarkadhish Temple, despite being his consort. This myth explains the separation of the temples and adds emotional depth to your visit.

Temple Architecture

Built in sand-colored stone, featuring intricate carvings of gods, goddesses, and celestial beings.

The temple is relatively small but artistically rich.

It features a main sanctum (garbhagriha) housing the idol of Rukmini Devi, adorned with beautiful ornaments and a golden crown.

Temple Timings

  • Morning: 6:00 AM to 12:00 PM
  • Evening: 4:00 PM to 9:00 PM
  • Darshan Duration: 15–30 minutes (not usually crowded)

Why Visit Rukmini Devi Temple?

It’s part of the Char Dham circuit of Gujarat.

Offers a peaceful and spiritual environment, away from crowds.

Beautiful architectural details perfect for photography and reflection.

Learn about lesser-known stories from Krishna’s life.

Combine it with your visit to Dwarkadhish Temple, Bet Dwarka, and Nageshwar Jyotirlinga.

How to Reach

  • By Road: Easily accessible via auto-rickshaw or cab from Dwarka.
  • By Train: Get down at Dwarka Railway Station and take local transport.
  • By Air: Nearest airport is Jamnagar (~130 km away).

Best Time to Visit

Visit between October and March when the weather is pleasant. Special rituals and decorations occur during Janmashtami, Diwali, and Rukmini Ashtami.

Travel Tips

  • Wear modest and comfortable clothing.
  • Photography is allowed outside, but ask before taking photos inside.
  • Combine your visit with Dwarkadhish Temple for a full spiritual experience.
  • Don't forget to drink the holy water (Ganga jal) offered at the temple.
